gloss: solo customer; person dining or traveling alone

definitions.explanation: A polite term used in restaurants and service contexts for a customer who comes alone.

definitions.gloss: person who enjoys doing things alone; single person
definitions.explanation: A broader cultural term for someone who comfortably does activities alone, such as dining, traveling, or going to the movies solo. Can also refer to an unmarried person.

examples.japanese: お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}ですか？
お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}、こちらへどうぞ。
examples.english: Party of one, right this way please.

examples.japanese: このレストランはお{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{大歓迎|だいかんげい}です。
examples.english: This restaurant warmly welcomes solo diners.

examples.japanese: お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{旅行|りょこう}が{人気|にんき}だ。
{最近|さいきん}はお{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{焼肉|やきにく}も{珍|めずら}しくない。
examples.english: These days, going to a yakiniku restaurant alone isn't unusual.

examples.japanese: お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{向|む}けのサービスが{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Services catering to solo customers are increasing.

notes:
Sense 1 is the original service-industry usage heard at restaurant entrances. Sense 2 developed as a cultural trend word describing the growing acceptance of doing activities alone in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}ですか？ — standard restaurant greeting
- お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{歓迎|かんげい} — solo customers welcome
- お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{席|せき} — solo seating
- お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{旅行|りょこう} — solo travel
- お{一人|ひとり}{様|さま}{焼肉|やきにく} — eating yakiniku alone

The term has a positive connotation in modern usage, reflecting a shift away from the idea that doing things alone is lonely or embarrassing.
